Laura / team — attaching a short FAQ and a draft plain-language paragraph. High level points: 
- Subprocessors: we list categories rather than every vendor in customer‑facing copy; link to full subprocessor PDF in the Console/DPA download. Example categories: cloud compute & storage (AWS/GCP/Azure), CDN/edge caching, observability/monitoring, payment processors (for billing), and managed security services.
- Access controls: describe least‑privilege, role-based access, strict contractual data access limits, and regular access reviews. Avoid naming infra teams.
- Transfers: we state we store and process in regions customers select where supported; for EU data we offer EU-region hosting and rely on SCCs + contractual safeguards for transfers; keys are customer‑managed for Private deployments (note: not for hosted unless customer purchases dedicated key option).

I trimmed legalese but left an excerpt that maps to our DPA. If you accept wording we can publish to Console FAQ and link the full DPA + subprocessor PDF.

Draft paragraph (150 words max):
"Redwood’s hosted API processes requests in the cloud providers and regions you select. We limit subprocessor access to only what’s necessary to run the service — e.g., cloud compute and storage, edge caching, monitoring, and payments — and bind those vendors contractually to the same data protections we provide in our DPA. Access is limited by role, audited, and restricted to operational needs. For customers with EU data residency requirements, we offer EU-region hosting where possible and protect transfers using standard contractual clauses and encryption in transit and at rest. If you need tighter controls, we support Dedicated capacity and Private deployments with customer-managed keys and additional contractual provisions. For a complete list of subprocessors, please download the DPA subprocessor list in the Console."

Attachment: console-privacy-summary-draft.md
Attachment: DPA_subprocessors_2026.pdf

Thanks — quick infra notes to keep the copy accurate: 
- Hosted API: ephemeral KV and prefix caches are resident in the serving region for low-latency; we do not persist prompt/response pairs to long-term analytics storage by default.
- Telemetry: aggregated telemetry is sent to our monitoring pipeline (vendor category: observability) and is pseudonymized; raw customer content is only retained per configured retention policies or when customers opt into debug logs.
- EU-region hosting: available on most models but some very large models are only in us-west-2 for capacity — we should call that out as "region availability varies by model" so customers expecting total EU-residency can request Dedicated or Private.

If you want, I can add a one-liner about debug logs being opt‑in and retention default (30 days) for hosted.

Marcus Lin
VP, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Samir — thanks for the note and the timeline. Attached is a short FAQ and a plain‑English paragraph we use in the Console (plus the full subprocessor list). Key points in plain language: 

- Data processing region: for hosted API, requests are processed in cloud regions you select where available; region availability varies by model.
- Who can access data: only essential subprocessors (cloud compute & storage, edge cache/CDN, monitoring/observability, and payment processors for billing) have access and are contractually bound to our DPA protections.
- Transfers & safeguards: for EU data residency we offer EU-region hosting where supported; otherwise transfers are covered by SCCs and encryption in transit/at rest. For customers who need more control, Dedicated or Private deployments provide stronger isolation and customer-managed keys.
